it: As your show New Rituals at HEK closes, what reflections do you have? What rituals are you hoping this show might actually change for audiences?

What rituals do you hope New Rituals might change for audiences?

Ritual versus addiction reminds me of Yuk Hui. One of his big ideas is recursion and contingency: recursion being feedback loops and then contingency just being information. He talks about the difference between a circle and a spiral: a circle is like a loop but you always go back to the same place and so you don’t really move. A spiral is also a loop but propelled by its interaction with the outside world.

How does Yuk Hui’s circle-versus-spiral idea relate to ritual and addiction?

New Rituals also aligns with Hui’s calls for a more pluralistic interpretation of technology. He staunchly opposes Silicon Valley tech monoculture. What’s the role of ritual in demonstrating resistance? I’m thinking of works in the show like Skawennati’s Mohawk ceremony in a Californian game engine, Sian Fan’s Tamagotchi-amulet and Ichihara’s mourning devices.

What role does ritual play in resisting Silicon Valley tech monoculture?

It’s the horseshoe effect where the two extremes curve back around and meet on re-enchantment. It speaks to society’s broader confusion about how to respond to AI. The hate is quite vocal but ChatGPT is by far the most downloaded app of the last twenty months. Gemini and Claude are in the top twenty. New Rituals seems to make sense of this by approaching AI through ideas of god and the apocalypse.

Does New Rituals find middle ground between rejecting and worshipping technology?

This sense that we’re actually re gressing thanks to technology directly counters the early tech optimism of thinkers like Stewart Brand and Roy Ascott. They had clear visions of what technology could be and were very optimistic. Fast forward to 2026, wah-wah. In the mid-90s Ascott was calling on artists to be the ones to show us the way with tech. In 2026, should artists be showing us the way or leading us away?
